drills.q: In one sentence each: what do the backbone, objective, and distillation axes control in generative media?
drills.a: Backbone (U-Net vs DiT): how well quality scales with compute and how flexibly modalities fit in. Objective (epsilon-prediction vs flow matching): path geometry, step requirements, determinism, likelihood. Distillation (LCM/Turbo/PFM): how few sampling steps you can afford and what quality tax they carry.

drills.q: Quote DiT-XL/2's headline numbers versus ADM-U.
drills.a: FID 2.27 on ImageNet 256x256 at 119 Gflops/sample vs ADM-U's 742 Gflops for worse results; at 512x512, FID 3.04 at 525 Gflops vs ADM-U's 3.85 at 2,813 — roughly 5x the compute efficiency.

drills.q: Write the CFM loss used in flow matching.
drills.a: MSE between the network's velocity prediction v(x_t,t) and the constant target x1-x0, where x_t=(1-t)x0+t*x1 is the linear interpolation of noise x0 and data x1. Lipman et al. showed this regression's gradient equals the intractable marginal-flow objective's.

drills.q: A teammate doubles denoising steps from 25 to 50 expecting better outputs. What does the DiT evidence say?
drills.a: Be skeptical: DiT showed model compute beats sampling compute — L/2 at 1000 steps (80.7 Tflops/image) LOST to XL/2 at 128 steps (15.2 Tflops), FID 23.7 vs 25.9. Extra steps can't fix a backbone-limited model; they reliably double inference cost. If quality plateaus, change backbone/data, not the sampler count.

drills.q: If interpolation paths are straight lines, why doesn't one Euler step sample exactly? And what fixes it?
drills.a: Because the marginal velocity field averages over all couplings through a point and is generally nonlinear even though each conditional path is linear; independent pairings create crossing curves. Rectified flow fixes it by re-pairing samples through the trained model and retraining — about two rounds make trajectories nearly straight enough for one-step Euler sampling.

drills.q: Explain why one-step consistency students produce blurry rather than noisy images, and how PFM addresses it.
drills.a: Coarse integration turns the regression into predicting a conditional expectation whose minimizer averages modes — soft blends instead of crisp picks (mean-seeking). PFM supervises decoded predictions in a pretrained perceptual feature space, shifting the minimizer toward mode-seeking, enabling sharp 4-8 step flow generation without any teacher model.

drills.q: You must cut video-generation cost ~5x without changing vendors. Rank the levers and their costs.
drills.a: 1) Distilled checkpoints (50 to 4-8 steps, ~6x measured, quality tax below 4 steps); 2) duration/resolution ladders with draft-then-refine (tokens scale with frames x area); 3) stronger temporal VAE compression; 4) batching/caching/off-peak scheduling. Keep a >=4-step floor because subjective quality collapses visibly beneath it.

drills.q: Outputs look burnt and oversaturated after switching to a guidance-distilled checkpoint. Diagnosis and fix?
drills.a: Classic excessive-guidance signature: CFG pushes samples off-manifold. In a distilled model guidance is baked in (e.g., frozen w=9.0), so there's no live knob — lower guidance if available, otherwise switch checkpoints/tiers rather than hunting for a dial that no longer exists.

drills.q: Where does Sora's spacetime patch idea fit the DiT story, and what breaks first as videos get longer?
drills.a: Spacetime patches are the video entry point: latent spatiotemporal cubes become tokens so the same ViT-style DiT scales across resolutions/durations — no per-format architectures. As length grows, quadratic attention over exploding token counts breaks first, plus temporal-consistency/world-model failures (object permanence), motivating sparse/MoE/linear attention and hierarchical approaches.

drills.q: Your team wants to fine-tune a generator on 5k domain images: DiT or U-Net? Defend briefly.
drills.a: At 5k images scaling-law advantages are irrelevant — transfer decides it: fine-tune whichever pretrained family matches your domain, license, and tooling; both ecosystems are mature. The U-Net-vs-DiT war matters at pretraining scale, not fine-tuning scale; claiming otherwise misapplies frontier-scale evidence to small-data regimes.

drills.q: What evidence would convince you one-step generation has truly matched multi-step quality?
drills.a: A method matching teacher distributions on diversity/tail-fidelity metrics (not headline FID alone) at one-two steps, demonstrated at video scale where temporal coherence compounds per-frame averaging failures. PFM itself admits degradation below two steps — structural mode-seeking loss isn't yet solved, only relocated.

drills.q: Name three things that break in production video pipelines that image pipelines never face.
drills.a: Temporal artifacts (flicker, object-permanence errors across frames), cost explosion from token counts growing linearly with frames (steps x tokens economics), and character/identity consistency across shots requiring reference conditioning or seed discipline. Plus prompt drift over long durations.
